mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 5.25% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 4.0% for three consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately compressing corporate margins and driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive two-month decline in GDPC1 signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in INDPRO below 97 for three consecutive months signals weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in HOUST and a fall in RSAFS over one month indicates increased housing demand with reduced savings, suggesting consumer spending reallocation toward housing, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous month AND RSAFS < previous month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in FEDFUNDS below 3.0% combined with a concurrent rise in CPIAUCSL above 3.0% for two months signals a monetary loosening in an inflationary environment, which historically has produced mixed but often positive equity returns over the next 60 trading days due to rate-cut optimism.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 3.0% AND CPIAUCSL > 3.0% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent fall in PAYEMS below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals broad-based employment weakness, which typically precedes negative equity returns over the next 60 trading days due to earnings downgrades.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between rising GDPC1 and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days in expansionary regimes, as stronger demand typically boosts earnings expectations and market sentiment.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.3%) in at least 55% of quarters when GDPC1 is rising.
